subject: business-studies
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each). Section B: questions 21–35 have two parts of 1 mark each.
Section C: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 5-mark answers in 80–120 words.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) It is not always necessary for a businessman to make the best possible use of materials. (b) Businessmen should use profits only for their own living.
questions.answer:
(a) False — best use of resources is an economic objective of business.
(b) False — profits should also be ploughed back for growth and used for the welfare of employees and society.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Activities performed with the objective of earning money are known as ________ activities. (b) The terms and conditions of employment are decided by the ________.
questions.answer:
(a) economic
(b) employer

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Traditional business always requires physical presence, whereas e-commerce does not. (b) B2C e-commerce involves transactions between businesses only.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — B2C is business to consumer; business to business is B2B.

questions.q: The business assets of an organisation are worth ₹90,000 but its unpaid debts are ₹1,20,000. In a sole proprietorship, what can the creditors do?
questions.answer:
(a) Take the ₹90,000 of business assets.
(b) Recover the balance ₹30,000 from the proprietor's personal property, because his liability is unlimited.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The minimum paid-up capital to start a private limited company was ₹ ________. (b) The liability of the members of a cooperative society is ________.
questions.answer:
(a) 1 lakh (under the Companies Act, 1956; the 2013 Act as amended has no minimum)
(b) limited

questions.q: Best answer: (a) Suman needs leave from work — which method of communication will she use? (b) Is communicating with pictures, symbols and diagrams visual communication?
questions.answer:
(a) Written communication — a leave application.
(b) Yes, it is visual communication.

questions.q: A digital payment system lets a user transact with Aadhaar number and fingerprint or iris; the account must be linked to Aadhaar. (a) Name the system. (b) Why is it considered safe?
questions.answer:
(a) AEPS — Aadhaar Enabled Payment System.
(b) It uses biometric authentication, which cannot easily be copied.

questions.q: A Mumbai company shipping textiles to Dubai buys an insurance policy valid only for this particular trip, regardless of the time taken. (a) Identify the type of marine policy. (b) For what kind of insurance is it mostly used?
questions.answer:
(a) Voyage policy.
(b) Cargo insurance.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) A wholesaler is an important link between the producer and the ________. (b) A retailer acts as a ________ between the wholesaler and the ultimate consumer.
questions.answer:
(a) retailer
(b) link (connecting link)

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Advertisements on buses and trains are known as ________ displays. (b) The primary objective of advertising is to create ________ for products.
questions.answer:
(a) vehicular (transit)
(b) demand

questions.q: Answer in one word: (a) What is the movement to protect consumer interests called? (b) Who can file a complaint in a consumer court?
questions.answer:
(a) Consumerism
(b) A consumer (also a registered consumer association or the government)

questions.q: Match: (a) Advertisements falsely represent a product as of superior quality (b) Stocks are intentionally held back — (i) hoarding (ii) sale of duplicates (iii) misleading advertisement (iv) false weights and measures
questions.answer:
(a) — (iii) misleading advertisement
(b) — (i) hoarding
(Measuring sticks with false markings — (iv) false weights and measures; goods showing a mark of superior quality — (ii) sale of duplicates.)

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) A goldsmith cannot be self-employed as he must work under a jeweller. (b) Some capital is needed even to provide an individualised service for a price.
questions.answer:
(a) False — a goldsmith can run his own workshop.
(b) True

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Entrepreneurs are gamblers. (b) An entrepreneur generates employment for others.
questions.answer:
(a) False — they take calculated risks.
(b) True

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) An individual who initiates, creates and manages a new business is called an ________. (b) Entrepreneurship is a ________ activity.
questions.answer:
(a) entrepreneur
(b) creative (risk-bearing)

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Give two examples each of economic and non-economic activities.
questions.answer:
Economic: a teacher teaching in a school for a salary; a shopkeeper selling goods.
Non-economic: a mother cooking for her family; a person doing charity or social service.

questions.q: Explain any two advantages of e-commerce.
questions.answer:
(1) Wider choice and market — customers can choose from products all over the world and sellers reach a global market.
(2) Cost saving — no showrooms or large godowns and fewer employees, so goods can be sold at lower prices.

questions.q: State two disadvantages of a joint stock company.
questions.answer:
(1) Difficult and expensive formation with many legal formalities.
(2) Lack of secrecy — accounts must be published.
(Also: delay in decisions; separation of ownership and control may lead to misuse.)

or.q: State two disadvantages of a multinational company.
or.answer:
(1) They may harm small domestic industries that cannot compete.
(2) They send large profits to their home country, causing an outflow of foreign exchange.
(Also: exploitation of natural resources; interference in local affairs.)

questions.q: What is video-conferencing?
questions.answer: Video-conferencing is a form of teleconferencing in which people at different places can hear and also see each other while talking, using cameras, screens and telecommunication or Internet links.

questions.q: A publisher sells books to a wholesaler who sells to local bookstores. Name the channel and the role of the wholesaler.
questions.answer:
Channel: Producer (publisher) → Wholesaler → Retailer (bookstores) → Consumer — an indirect, two-level channel.
The wholesaler buys in bulk, stores the books and distributes them in smaller lots to bookstores, often on credit.

or.q: How do retailers help in stabilising prices?
or.answer: Retailers keep stocks and buy regularly from wholesalers, so goods are available steadily; by informing wholesalers about demand they help match supply with demand, which keeps prices stable.

questions.q: Explain the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986.
questions.answer: It set up the Bureau of Indian Standards (in place of the ISI) to protect consumers. BIS formulates quality standards for goods and certifies products that meet them, allowing them to carry the ISI mark.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe any three types of industries with examples.
questions.answer:
(1) Primary — production with the help of nature: agriculture, fishing.
(2) Extractive — drawing out goods from soil, air or water: mining, oil, timber.
(3) Manufacturing — converting raw materials into finished goods: sugar, textiles, paper.
(Also genetic — nurseries, poultry; construction — roads, dams; service — hotels.)

questions.q: Explain the elements of the communication process.
questions.answer:
(1) Sender — the person who starts communication and sends the message.
(2) Message — the subject matter: facts, ideas, feelings or information.
(3) Medium — the means that carries the message (letter, telephone, e-mail).
(4) Receiver — the person who receives the message.
(5) Feedback — the receiver's response directed back to the sender; it shows the message was understood.

questions.q: What is an ATM? How does it help bank customers?
questions.answer:
An Automated Teller Machine is an electronic machine installed by banks at convenient places.
It helps customers: (1) withdraw cash at any time, 24 × 7; (2) check balance and get a mini statement; (3) deposit cash and transfer funds without going to the branch.

or.q: State any three secondary functions of a commercial bank.
or.answer:
(1) Agency functions — collecting cheques, dividends and interest, paying premiums and bills for customers.
(2) Issuing demand drafts and traveller's cheques.
(3) Safe deposit lockers and safe custody of valuables; letters of credit; foreign exchange.

questions.q: How do retailers help consumers? Give any three ways.
questions.answer:
(1) Regular supply of a variety of goods near the home, in small quantities.
(2) Personal service — guidance on quality and use, home delivery and credit facility.
(3) Attractive display and information about new products, helping consumers choose.

or.q: State any three services of wholesalers to manufacturers.
or.answer:
(1) Bulk buying — they buy in large quantities, so the manufacturer is spared many small orders.
(2) Storage — they keep goods in their own warehouses, relieving the manufacturer of storage.
(3) Finance and information — they often pay in cash or in advance and pass on market information about demand and tastes.

questions.q: State any three points on the importance of advertising.
questions.answer:
(1) It educates customers about products and their uses.
(2) It creates demand for new products and maintains demand for existing ones.
(3) It increases sales and assists salesmen, and helps the firm face competition.

questions.q: Explain the importance of choosing a career.
questions.answer:
(1) It lays the foundation of one's working life and shapes life-style, values and habits.
(2) In a competitive world the right early choice saves time and avoids frustration and frequent job changes.
(3) It helps a person discover his abilities and use them, leading to satisfaction and progress.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: 'This business exists under Hindu law and is governed by the law of succession.' Identify it and state its features.
questions.answer:
Joint Hindu Family (HUF) business.
(1) Membership by birth — coparceners of three generations.
(2) Management by the Karta, the eldest member.
(3) Liability — unlimited for the Karta, limited to their share for other members.
(4) Continuity — unaffected by the death of any member, including the Karta.
(5) No registration needed; no maximum number of members.

questions.q: HDFC Bank offers many accounts. Geeta, a businesswoman, chose an account with the most liquid deposits and no limit on the number of transactions; her mother opened one for her savings with cheque facility; her brother Kartik deposits ₹3,000 every month for two years. (a) Identify the accounts. (b) Explain two other types of account.
questions.answer:
(a) Geeta — current deposit account; her mother — savings bank account; Kartik — recurring deposit account.
(b) Fixed deposit account — a lump sum kept for a fixed period at a higher interest rate.
Multiple option (flexi) deposit — a savings account where amounts above a limit move automatically to a fixed deposit and earn more interest.

or.q: Anil learns of an account at SBI in which amounts above a limit are transferred automatically to a fixed deposit, combining the benefits of savings and FD. Identify and explain it.
or.answer: Multiple option deposit account (flexi or sweep account). It works like a savings account for deposits and withdrawals, but when the balance exceeds a set limit the excess is automatically moved into a fixed deposit, earning the higher FD interest; when needed, money comes back from the FD to the savings account. So the customer gets both liquidity and higher interest.

questions.q: What is meant by consumerism? Explain any two responsibilities of a consumer.
questions.answer:
Consumerism is a movement by consumers and their associations to protect consumers from unfair and dishonest practices and to create awareness of their rights.
(1) Self-help — an informed consumer protects himself better than anyone else.
(2) Proper use of products and reasonable claims — misuse or exaggerated claims are irresponsible.

questions.q: Vivek, a finance manager, decides to start his own business. Explain five qualities he should have to be a successful entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
(1) Initiative — act quickly on opportunities.
(2) Willingness to take calculated risk.
(3) Ability to learn from experience.
(4) Motivation and hard work.
(5) Self-confidence and decision-making ability.
